transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Sentinel Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Infra), Sara Bennet (PM)

Summary:
- POC scoping focused on integration plan: SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, and structured output validation.
- Success criteria discussed: latency, cost, quality, and operational measurements (tracing, logging).
- Workload sizing and benchmark plan agreed: seed prompts + 1-week benchmark on Dedicated, aim for p95 latency and cost targets.
- Next steps: pricing + SOW, benchmark harness, customer to share logs and VPC access.

Topics:
- Integration: SDKs and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function calling, schema validation, streaming outputs.
- Workload sizing: avg qps, peak bursts, typical sequence lengths, token mix.
- Benchmarks: what to measure, how to run (with/without caching), data obfuscation.
- Timeline and success criteria for 4-week pilot.

Transcript:
00:00 Maya: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i'll let Diego and i intro quickly.
00:08 Diego: hey all, diego here, i'll be running the technical bits for the poc and the benchmark harness.
00:12 Priya: hey priya here, thanks. we're excited — we've been looking at options for lower latency inference for our realtime enrichment pipeline.
00:21 Liam: liam from infra, i'll be the one coordinating VPC and network stuff.
00:24 Sara: sara, product, here to make sure success criteria map to product goals.
00:30 Maya: quick agenda — we want to align on success criteria, sizing, bench plan and integration surface (sdk/openai-compat, function-calling, structured json outputs). also timeline for the 4 week poc.
00:44 Priya: sounds good. fyi our main requirement is p95 latency under load, and we need deterministic structured outputs for downstream consumers, plus SSO/audit for security.
00:56 Diego: noted. can you share numbers — avg and peak qps, typical prompt seq len, token mix?
01:02 Priya: sure — currently our enrichment API sees avg 8 rps per region, typical peak to 60 rps, but during campaigns jumps to 120 rps for short bursts. average request yields ~220 tokens out, prompts avg 80 tokens.
01:18 Maya: okay so for sizing we should plan for steady 8 qps and be able to handle sustained 60 qps and bursts to 120 qps. for poc we can target a single region on dedicated capacity.
01:28 Sara: what's the cost ballpark? we have budget constraints, want to keep per inference cost competitive with our current hosted provider.
01:34 Maya: we'll provide dedicated pricing in the SOW, rough guidance now: with batching and KV caching you'd typically see token cost reduced — but we'll put explicit per-token and per-hour capacity numbers in the doc.
01:45 Priya: also the structured output — we need function-like calls that return strict json schemas; we have parsers downstream that are brittle.
01:54 Diego: Redwood supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints and function-calling semantics, we can register JSON schemas and validate outputs on the runtime side; there's a streaming mode too so you can pipe partial responses to downstream systems.
02:06 Priya: when you say "register" is that a compile-time check or runtime validation?
02:10 Diego: both; we can validate at runtime and optionally run a schema conformance check during generation end-of-stream. small caveat — sometimes transcriptions show "KV cash" in logs but runtime validates the JSON payload.
02:22 Sara: ha, ok. on onboarding — do you have SDKs?
02:28 Maya: yes, SDKs for python, node, and a lightweight go client. they're OpenAI-compatible so minimal changes — same endpoints, but we also offer a native client that exposes dedicated features like kernel tuning and batch hints.
02:43 Priya: we use a mix of python backend workers and a go service for realtime. will the SDKs cover streaming + function calls?
02:49 Diego: yes. streaming is supported via the SDK and via raw http with chunked responses; function calling is supported via the OpenAI-compat payloads (we map schema defs into runtime validators).
02:59 Liam: for private deployments — we may require a VPC/on-prem option because of compliance. how does Redwood Private work re: KMS?
03:07 Maya: Redwood Private offers a private control plane and an on-prem option; integrates with KMS/HSM and we can plug into customer-managed KMS. we'll include SOC 2 and encryption docs in the security packet.
03:18 Priya: that's good. for the poc we prefer Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) to simplify benchmarking but want the option to evaluate Private later.
03:26 Maya: makes sense — Dedicated will let us guarantee latency and capacity for the benchmark window.
03:30 Diego: about benchmarks — we recommend running two passes: 1) profiler pass at low qps to validate p95/p99 latency per sequence length, 2) load pass to simulate sustained and burst workloads. we'll instrument traces, token cost, and quality metrics (exact-match for structured JSON fields + semantic checks).
03:47 Priya: how many seed prompts do you need?
03:50 Diego: 150–300 prompts that cover your common paths; include edge cases where you expect long tail failures. also provide a mapping of critical fields to assert in outputs.
03:58 Priya: we can do 200 prompts, i'll include example failing cases.
04:02 Sara: timeline — are we looking at 4 weeks?
04:05 Maya: typical pilot is 4 weeks: week 0 onboarding + infra; week 1 profiler + schema tuning; week 2 load tests and caching configs; week 3 run final benchmarks and review. can compress to 3 weeks if customer provides VPC access and logs quickly.
04:20 Priya: we can aim for 4 weeks, want final report with recommendations and suggested quantization / batching profiles.
04:28 Diego: we'll include model/quantization recommendations in the report — e.g., int8 profiles, kernel selection notes. note that some of the GPU kernels behave better at certain sequence lengths — we'll capture that in benchmarks.
04:40 Priya: about telemetry — need per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdown.
04:45 Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and traces. we'll enable retention per your compliance needs.
04:54 Liam: network testing — we need to test egress rules and our NAT throughput; will you run from our dev VPC?
04:59 Diego: yes we'll ask you for a dev VPC and a test host; we can run the load generator from a host inside your VPC or from Redwood Dedicated in-region and measure network hop and egress costs.
05:12 Sara: any blockers you're seeing for us to start?
05:15 Priya: main blockers: security review (SOC2 docs), KMS handshake for Private later, and we need clear SLOs in the SOW.
05:24 Maya: we'll attach SOC2 packet and our KMS integration notes, and the SOW will list target SLOs for the pilot.
05:30 Diego: one more technical note — for structured output we recommend the function-calling + schema validation path. if you need deterministic outputs, we can run low-temp decoding and apply prefix caching for common templates.
05:43 Priya: will that affect latency?
05:46 Diego: caching reduces compute by reusing KV cache for common prefixes — it typically helps latency and cost; low-temp decoding doesn't materially add overhead but can increase p99 variance, so we'll quantify both.
05:58 Maya: recap of success criteria, as discussed:
- Performance: p95 latency target < 300ms for typical 220-token outputs under steady 8 qps; p95 under sustained 60 qps should be within 1.2x of that number.
- Cost: target token cost comparable to current provider — we'll agree a per-token target in the SOW.
- Quality: structured JSON exact-match on critical fields >= 98% for seed set; semantic checks for optional fields.
- Ops: full tracing, per-request token breakdown, and audit logs available.
06:34 Priya: that looks good, i want the 98% threshold documented.
06:38 Maya: yes we'll add that to success criteria in the SOW.
06:41 Sara: ok, next steps?
06:43 Maya: action items — i'll send pricing + SOW and attach security docs; diego will prepare the benchmark harness and a sample run plan; priya and liam will share logs and VPC access. we'll target benchmark start the week of 2026-05-04.
06:58 Priya: good, we'll aim to provide artifacts this week.
07:02 Maya: cool thanks everyone; we'll follow up with calendar invites for the kickoff and the benchmark windows. 
07:09 End of call.

Shared artifacts referenced:
- POC checklist + SOW template: https://redwood.example.com/poc-checklist (shared live)
- Benchmark harness repo (private link to be shared by Diego)
- Security packet (SOC2, encryption, KMS notes) — will be attached to SOW

Notes on transcription quality: some spoken fragments abbreviated, occasional mis-hear (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, "V-P-C" spelled out).
